question.prompt: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be the following sums of arithmetic sequences: \[\begin{aligned} X &= 10+12+14+\cdots+100,\\ Y &= 12+14+16+\cdots+102. \end{aligned}\] What is the value of \(Y - X?\)

solutions.explanation:
Both sums contain every even number from \(12\) through \(100\). Grouping those shared terms avoids computing either long sum. Let
\[
S=12+14+\cdots+100.
\]
Then \(X=10+S\) and \(Y=S+102\), so
\[
Y-X=(S+102)-(10+S)=102-10=92.
\]
Thus the answer is \(92\), choice A.
solutions.title: Cancel the shared terms
